The mayors and city clerks of Milwaukee, Madison, Racine and Kenosha were also named in the lawsuit, as well as the Milwaukee and Dane County Clerks, the Milwaukee Election Director, the Exe Director of the Milwaukee Election Commission, and Gov Tony Evers.

The lawsuit goes on to say that despite the name of the plan, it didn’t apply to the whole state, it was just for those five cities. Those city officials were then said to have planned to use drop-boxes to make the return of absentee ballots easier in the state’s largest cities.

As an attorney who works in federal court, appellate federal court, is a member of the Supreme Court Bar, and having been a federal judicial law clerk (though not at the S.Ct.), this isn't how it works.

First, The Supreme Court is one of the most locked down, secretive places on earth. You do not gossip, you do not leak. You are charged with some of the greatest secrets (what the Court's ruling is to be), and no one (law clerks, secretaries, clerks, janitors) would betray that trust and oath.

Second, OP's post talks about denying the amicus briefs. There are two things (maybe three things), going on right now.

1) The plaintiffs (Texas) filed a motion for leave to file a complaint. Because the court had original jurisdiction over a controversy between the states, this is a type of case that get filed in the first instance at the Supreme Court. But they still have to decide to "take" it. You can file what you want, but we can still deny to hear the case.

2) "all" that happened today at 3 pm is that the defendants (the bad states) had until 3 pm today to file their response to THAT motion (should the case even be taken). IF you think that 9 justices of the Supreme Court have dropped everything, and read ALL of those briefs, and already voted and decided, you are wrong. They are way more scholarly than that in what might be the most important constitutional question to ever come before the Court. No, they are just sitting down now to read those, at the earliest, if not tomorrow.

3) But also today MANY entities (other states, legislatures, special interest groups, the republican party, etc.) are also seeking leave to file Amicus briefs (friend of the court). While not party to the case, these groups think that they have something to add that the Court should consider. Your amicus brief has to be accepted. You can't just file stuff.

I would not be surprised if there was denial of some of these amicus briefs--the case is complicated enough and on a short time line enough without 100 extra briefs that they are also bound to read and consider. So OP might be right that there is disagreement about that, and that they might have voted on that today (yes to this one, no to that one, or let's just say no to them all, versus we should say yes to them all). But that is certainly not a decision on the merits, or even a decision on taking the case for consideration. That is a housekeeping matter.

To the point that they have already considered this case on the merits and decided, that has certainly not happened. These people are way too thoughtful and scholarly for that. And fair.

To your point that somehow three (liberal) judges have thrown a hissy fit that if the Court takes the case to consider it, that they will refuse to participate, that is ridiculous. That is not how they work. If a case is taken that you thought should not be, you would certainly participate in order to right that issue, argue against it, write your dissent, etc. You don't boycott the Supreme Court on which you sit.

Could it be there are some judges thinking of RECUSING themselves (which only they can do, and they cannot be made to by anyone). That could be happening.

There could be considerations going on as to whether ACB should recuse herself (which we heard so much about during the hearings). Or even Justice Thomas (because of his history with Biden). That last one, because the Court is sitting in this case as the first level (and only level) court, his connection to Biden is one that as a trial court judge, a party would bring a motion for Thomas to recuse himself because Thomas could be biased against Biden, the ultimate winner (or loser) depending on how the case is ruled upon.

So, as interesting as this all sounds, like some Grisham novel, this is not what is happening.

It's a bunch of law clerks, pouring over these briefs, for all of 5 hours now. The justices are doing it too (not quite as feverishly). The Court meets in conference on Wednesday and Friday afternoons. Maybe some of this conversation will be had tomorrow. But there is massive work and review and reading that has to go on to be able to even consider whether they WILL consider this case.

The S. Ct. is one of the most regimented places on earth. They are dealing with this case in the normal course, no matter how extraordinary we all feel it is, or it may in fact be.

To the final point, that if three justices were in fact having a hissy fit and refusing to sit in on the case. First, we will never know it was a hissy fit. At the most it would be an announcement that they had elected to recuse themselves with no further explanation (which nothing requires them to explain themselves). None of the other justices would throw their colleagues under the bus like that. The Chief Justice would never allow anyone to be derelict in their duties. Judicial conduct codes do not allow it.

But IF they were, the only means to remove a federal judge (who serves for life) is through impeachment, just like impeachment of a president. While over the years there have been a fair number of federal lower court judges impeached, only 1 justice has every been impeached by the House, and then he was acquitted in the Senate (Samuel Chase 1805).
